summary: Allowed Ferdinand Schwarz to be appointed permanently as an unclassified laborer in the Government Printing Office.
Set aside additional lots on the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah as townsites, adding them to the town lands already reserved by a proclamation of July 31, 1905.
Shrank a reservoir site on the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah to only the lands needed to protect the water supply, returning the rest to their earlier status.
Amended the civil service rules so a private secretary or confidential clerk to the Post Office Department's purchasing agent could be hired without examination.
Revoked an executive order of December 9, 1852, that had reserved certain lands in Michigan for lighthouse purposes.
Created the Holy Cross Forest Reserve on public timberland in Colorado, reserving it from settlement under the 1891 forest reserve law.
Reserved Santa Barbara Island, California, for lighthouse purposes.
Allowed May R. Proctor to be appointed to a position in the Government Printing Office without examination.
Reserved parcels of newly reclaimed harbor land in the city of Manila, Philippine Islands, for military purposes.
Gave employees of the Washington Navy Yard the day off for Labor Day, September 4, 1905.
Set the pay for members of the Advisory Board of Engineers working on plans for the Panama Canal.
Allowed Philip Cowen to be appointed immigrant inspector in the Immigration Service without a civil service examination.
Laid out the procedure for removing officers and employees serving on the Isthmus of Panama.
Reserved certain lands on Gravina and False Islands in Alaska for lighthouse purposes.
Changed the boundaries of the military reservation at Fort San Pedro in Iloilo, on Panay in the Philippine Islands.
Allowed John B. Goff and D. P. Wells to be appointed assistant forest rangers in the Forest Service without examination.
Set out regulations for how the Congressional Medal of Honor is to be presented.
Approved an acting Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve lands at Safety Harbor and Old Woman, Alaska, for the Signal Corps' military cable and telegraph lines.
Let Mary E. Enright be reinstated in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing despite the time limit on eligibility for reinstatement.
Established the Dixie Forest Reserve on public timberland in Utah, setting it apart from settlement.
Permitted W. E. Hall to move from the Isthmian Canal Service to a Class D clerkship in the Treasury Department, waiving civil service Rule X's six-month service requirement.
Enlarged the Madison Forest Reserve in Montana, adding public lands partly covered with timber and redrawing its boundaries.
Created the Big Belt Forest Reserve on public timberland in Montana and reserved it from settlement.
Established the Shasta Forest Reserve on public timberland in California, closing it to settlement.
Expanded the Lake Tahoe Forest Reserve with added timberland in California and Nevada and renamed it the Tahoe Forest Reserve.
Created the Tonto Forest Reserve on public timberland in the Territory of Arizona and reserved it from settlement.
Established the Hell Gate Forest Reserve on public timberland in Montana, setting the land aside from settlement.
Redrew the Lincoln Forest Reserve in the Territory of New Mexico, releasing some lands and adding others partly covered with timber; the released lands reopened to settlement.
Created the Portales Forest Reserve on public land in the Territory of New Mexico and reserved it from settlement.
Added timbered public lands in Montana to the Little Belt Mountains Forest Reserve, redrew its boundaries and changed its name.
Allowed Marjorie H. Young to be kept on and appointed as a clerk in the U.S. pension agency at Pittsburg, Pennsylvania, without a civil service examination.
Allowed Mrs. M. C. Miller to be appointed to a clerkship in the classified service without a civil service examination.
Amended the civil service rules so a private secretary to the Director of the Geological Survey could be appointed without examination.
Closed the western land district office at Kingfisher, Oklahoma Territory, and merged its lands, business and records into the eastern land district at Guthrie.
Set aside the Passage Key Reservation as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Created the Siskiwit Islands Reservation as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Established the Huron Islands Reservation as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Let Dessie M. Bowers of West Virginia be reinstated in any executive department, in view of her earlier service in the Department of Commerce and Labor.
Established the Jemez Forest Reserve on public lands in the Territory of New Mexico and reserved it from settlement.
Barred federal officers and employees from coaching anyone for Civil Service Commission examinations, making such coaching grounds for removal.
Banned the export of arms, ammunition and munitions of war from any port in the United States or Porto Rico to the Dominican Republic until further order.
Allowed Dollie A. Slayton of Montana, then in a temporary Census Bureau job, to be appointed to the Bureau's permanent clerical roll.
Let Julia P. Madeira of West Virginia, dropped from the Census Bureau during a long illness, be reinstated and transferred to the assayer's office of the mint at Denver.

Allowed inefficient or incapable classified employees to be removed without a hearing, provided the cause was put in writing, and permitted summary removal for misconduct witnessed by the President or a department head.
Allowed Charles Denby to be appointed chief clerk of the State Department without a civil service examination.
Exempted temporary field workers of the Bureau of Fisheries, paid from lump appropriations, from civil service examination.
Directed the Civil Service Commission to help set up competitive examinations, open to District of Columbia residents, for clerical jobs in the Recorder of Deeds office in Washington.
Abolished the Grand Fork land district in North Dakota and transferred it to the Devils Lake land district.
Approved the form of a proclamation reducing the Black Hills Forest Reserve in South Dakota.
Allowed Edward McCauley to become chief of the Post Office Department's Redemption Division without examination, given his experience as chief clerk of the Census Bureau.
Named Thursday, November 30, 1905, a national day of thanksgiving, giving thanks for bountiful crops and prosperity while urging Americans to own their shortcomings and strive to overcome them.
Reserved certain lands in California for use with the Point Sal lighthouse reservation.
Authorized extra pay for enlisted Navy men serving on submarine torpedo boats.

Extended examination requirements to every consulate general, consulate and commercial or consular agency paying at least $1,000 a year, filling vacancies by transfer, promotion, or examination of candidates the President selects.
Ordered that vacancies for secretaries of embassy or legation be filled by transfer or promotion within the foreign service, or by examination of candidates the President selects.
Created the Yuba Forest Reserve on public timberland in California and reserved it from settlement.
Applied the civil service rules on hiring laborers to workers at Indian warehouses.
Established the Breton Island Reservation in Louisiana.
Approved an acting Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve public land near Zamboanga, Mindanao, Philippine Islands, as a target range for the post.

Let the Civil Service Commission allow temporary Isthmian Canal Service appointments when no eligible with the needed skills is on its registers; these could become permanent on the Canal Commission's certificate.

Rewrote civil service Rule XII on removals: like penalties for like offenses, removal only to promote efficiency, written causes, and limits on the Civil Service Commission's power to investigate removals.
Exempted one tobacco examiner and one tea examiner in the Customs Service at the Port of Chicago from civil service examination.
Abolished the Bent land district in Colorado and transferred it to the Valley land district, with its office at Pueblo.
Approved an acting Secretary of War's recommendation to shrink the St. Michael Military Reservation and transfer the released lands to the Interior Department.
Allowed S. H. Alexander to be appointed a clerk in the Post Office Department without regard to the civil service rules.

Changed one word in the August 31, 1905, order so each Panama Canal Advisory Board engineer's $5,000 was due on completion of the board's "work" rather than its report, letting foreign members be paid before going home.
Allowed Marie L. Eastwood to be appointed to a permanent position in the Bureau of the Census, in view of her earlier satisfactory service there.
Amended the civil service rules to exempt cooks from examination.
Reserved certain lands in California for lighthouse purposes.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve public lands on Chilkat Inlet, Alaska, for the water supply of Fort William H. Seward.
Allowed Edna M. Peltz to be appointed permanently to a clerical position in the Pension Office without examination.
Abolished the Sidney land district in Nebraska and transferred it to the Western land district, with its office at North Platte.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve public lands at Keystone, Alaska, for a military telegraph.
Authorized the Isthmian Canal Commission to hold its quarterly session of January 1, 1906, in Washington, D.C.
Appointed a committee to plan an inquiry into sanitary conditions in government offices, aimed at preventing tuberculosis.
Made the assistant assayer position in each mint or assay office subject to civil service examination, striking it from the list of excepted positions.
Allowed Emily L. Genella to be reappointed in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without regard to the civil service rules.
Allowed Howard H. Belden to be appointed in any executive department after passing a noncompetitive examination.
Allowed Mary E. Owings to be appointed to a position in the Government Printing Office without examination.
Permitted thirteen special agents in the Bureau of the Census to transfer to competitive positions, putting them on the same footing as employees classified by act of Congress.
Let Katherine S. Todd transfer from the Bureau of Engraving and Printing to a clerkship in the office of the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, waiving civil service Rule X restrictions.

Exempted seasonal Agriculture Department guards, guides, cooks, packers, teamsters, choppers and skilled laborers hired during fire season from examination, capping their service at six months a year.
Allowed Anna F. McCormick, temporarily employed by the Isthmian Canal Commission, to be appointed there permanently.
Let Richard H. Williams be reinstated as an inspector of hulls of steam vessels despite the one-year limit in the civil service rules.
Allowed Nevil Monroe Hopkins to be appointed electrical engineer in the Navy's Bureau of Yards and Docks after a noncompetitive examination.

Added carpenters, cabinetmakers, painters, plumbers, electricians and related trades to the jobs exempt from the rule apportioning Washington appointments among the states by population, and dropped pages from the list.
Let Hattie R. McMullin be reinstated in a classified Interior Department position even though she had been out of the service more than a year.
Allowed Mrs. Mary E. Griffin to be reinstated in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without regard to the civil service rules.
Made a temporary appointment of Mrs. Charles (Florence E.) Broady.
Concerned the appointment of Howard H. Belden.
Cut U.S. duties on Swiss argols, brandies, still wines and vermuth, and artworks, matching Switzerland's removal of differential duties on American goods.
Abolished the Stockton land district in California and transferred it to the Sacramento land district.
Created the Jamestown Tercentennial Commission under a March 3, 1905, act celebrating the Jamestown settlement, naming cabinet members including Leslie M. Shaw and William H. Taft to serve.
Exempted stitch counters in the New York customs district from civil service examination.
Allowed Ralph Whitman, temporarily employed as an engineer draftsman with the Isthmian Canal Commission, to be appointed there permanently.
